gloss: turn aside, depart; (hiphil) remove, take away, put away
summary: To turn aside out of a course, and so to leave it: a traveller turns aside from the road to lodge or to look, Israel turns aside from the way Yahweh commanded, to the right or to the left, and the wise man turns away from evil. What departs is gone: the spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul, the plague from the garment, the scepter shall not depart from Judah. The hiphil makes something turn aside or go, the common word for remove and take away: a garment, a ring, the fat of an offering, foreign gods and high places, sickness, iniquity, the heart of stone, a king from his throne, a people from Yahweh's face. The noun סָרָה is a turning aside from Yahweh, revolt, spoken by false prophets.

words.gloss: turn aside, depart; be removed; (hiphil) remove, take away, put away
words.summary: About 300 times. The qal is the movement out of a line or course, and with מִן “from” the leaving of what one was in or with; the hiphil makes something leave, and is the ordinary word for remove. Its opposites are cleaving (דָּבַק) and returning (שׁוּב); its partner is נָטָה “incline, turn aside”.

stems.gloss: turn aside, turn in; turn away from; depart, cease, be removed

senses.gloss: turn aside from the road, turn in
senses.definition: To leave the road one is on and go aside to a place or a person: to lodge in a house, to see a sight, to sit down, to eat.

evidence.note: Lot to the messengers: “turn aside (סוּרוּ) to the house of your servant and spend the night … then you can go on your way.”
He pressed them hard, “and they turned aside (וַיָּסֻרוּ) to him and entered his house.”
“Let me turn aside (אָסֻרָה) and see this great sight”: Moses leaves his path to the bush.
“Yahweh saw that he turned aside to see.”
“They turned aside there to go in to lodge in Gibeah.”
Boaz to the redeemer passing by: “Turn aside, sit down here … and he turned aside and sat down.”
“As often as he passed by, he turned aside there to eat bread.”
Jael: “Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not fear.”
Wisdom calls, “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here”; Folly says the same (Pro 9:16).
Abner to Asahel, pursuing him: “Turn aside to your right or to your left.”
“I will go by the road, by the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left”: keeping to the road is the opposite.

senses.gloss: turn aside from Yahweh's way and commands
senses.definition: To leave the way Yahweh commanded, his commandments, or Yahweh himself: to go off the road, to the right or to the left. It is said of Israel making the calf, of kings who kept to Jeroboam's sins, and of all mankind.

evidence.note: “They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made themselves a molten calf.”
The same words, as Moses retells it.
“Be careful to do as Yahweh your God commanded you; do not turn aside to the right or to the left.”
“Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, that you may succeed.”
“Lest your heart be deceived, and you turn aside and serve other gods.”
The king shall not multiply wives, “that his heart not turn aside.”
“Do not turn aside from after Yahweh, but serve Yahweh with all your heart; do not turn aside after empty things” (v. 21).
“Cursed is the man who trusts in man … and whose heart turns aside from Yahweh.”
“From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you.”
“We have sinned … rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and from your judgments.”
“All have turned aside (הַכֹּל סָר), together they have become corrupt; there is none who does good”: quoted at Rom 3:12.
“All have turned aside (ἐξέκλιναν), together they have become worthless”, of Jews and Greeks alike.
Hezekiah “clung to Yahweh; he did not turn aside from after him, and kept his commandments”: cleaving is the opposite.
Josiah “walked in all the way of David his father and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.”
“He did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat”, the refrain of the kings of Israel.
In the everlasting covenant Yahweh will put his fear in their heart “so that they will not turn aside from me.”
“For grain and new wine they gather; they turn away from me.”
“Those who turn aside from me (Qere וְסוּרַי) shall be written in the earth, for they have forsaken Yahweh.”
The people to the prophets: “Turn aside from the way, leave the path, remove the Holy One of Israel from before us.”

senses.gloss: turn away from evil; depart from
senses.definition: To turn away from evil, or from wicked men, the grave and snares of death: the mark of one who fears Yahweh. As a command, “depart” from the unclean, from the tents of the wicked, or from the one who speaks.

evidence.note: Job “feared God and turned away from evil (וְסָר מֵרָע).”
“The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.”
“Fear Yahweh and turn away from evil.”
“By the fear of Yahweh one turns away from evil.”
“The highway of the upright is to turn away from evil.”
“To turn away from evil is an abomination to fools.”
“Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it”: quoted at 1Pe 3:11.
“Let him turn away (ἐκκλινάτω) from evil and do good.”
“He who turns away from evil makes himself a prey.”
“The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may turn away from the grave (שְׁאוֹל) below.”
“To turn away from the snares of death.”
“Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs.”
“Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing”; echoed at 2Co 6:17.
“Depart! Unclean!” they cried to them, “Depart, depart, do not touch!”
“Depart from me, all workers of iniquity”: the words of Mat 7:23 and Luk 13:27.
“Depart from me, evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God.”
“Men of blood, depart from me.”
The wicked to God: “Depart from us; we do not desire the knowledge of your ways.”
“Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart (ἀποστήτω) from unrighteousness”, after Num 16:5 and the departing of Num 16:26.

senses.gloss: depart, go away; cease, be removed
senses.definition: Of what was with or on someone: to leave, to be gone. Yahweh, his spirit, strength, a plague, a cloud, a yoke, jealousy, bitterness; with a negative, a thing that does not depart stays: the scepter from Judah, the sword from David's house, folly from a fool. Of high places and the like, “were not removed”.

evidence.note: “The spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul.”
“Yahweh was with him (David) and had departed from Saul.”
Saul: “God has departed from me and does not answer me any more.”
“If I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I shall become weak and be like any man.”
“He did not know that Yahweh had departed from him.”
“Woe to them when I depart from them.”
A garment washed, “and the plague has departed from them.”
“The cloud departed from over the tent.”
“Their shade has departed from them, and Yahweh is with us”: protection gone.
“His burden will depart from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck.”
“The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart.”
“My jealousy shall depart from you; I will be quiet and no more angry.”
Agag: “Surely the bitterness of death has departed.”
“The revelry of those who stretch themselves shall depart.”
“This has touched your lips; your iniquity is taken away (וְסָר), and your sin atoned for.”
“The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes.”
“My steadfast love shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul.”
“The sword shall never depart from your house.”
The poles “shall not be removed from it.”
“Even when he is old he will not depart from it.”
“His folly will not depart from him.”
“But the high places were not removed (לֹא סָרוּ).”
“Since the day Ephraim departed from Judah.”

senses.definition: The passive participle: one put aside or gone aside, a wife put away, the degenerate shoots of a foreign vine.

evidence.note: Zion: “I was bereaved and barren, an exile and put away (וְסוּרָה).”
“I planted you a choice vine … how then have you turned into the degenerate shoots (סוּרֵי) of a foreign vine?”: turned aside from what it was planted to be.

stems.gloss: remove, take away, take off; put away; turn aside, turn away

senses.definition: To take a thing off or away from where it was: a covering, a garment, a ring, armour, the fat and kidneys of an offering, a head.

evidence.note: “Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked.”
Tamar “took off her widow's garments from her and covered herself with a veil.”
“Pharaoh took his ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's hand.”
The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman.
Moses “would remove the veil until he came out”: echoed at 2Co 3:16.
David put off Saul's armour: “I cannot go with these.”
The kidneys and the lobe of the liver “he shall remove.”
“I will strike you down and take off your head.”
“Remove the filthy garments from him … I have taken your iniquity from you, and will clothe you with festal robes.”
The princes of the sea “will remove their robes.”

senses.gloss: put away foreign gods, idols and high places
senses.definition: To put away from among the people the gods, idols, Asherim and high places, the act of every return to Yahweh and every reform.

evidence.note: Jacob: “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves.”
“Fear Yahweh and serve him … and put away the gods your fathers served beyond the River.”
“They put away the foreign gods from among them and served Yahweh.”
“If you are returning to Yahweh with all your heart, put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth.”
Hezekiah “removed the high places and broke the pillars.”
Manasseh “removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of Yahweh.”
“I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth.”
Returned to the land, “they will remove from it all its detestable things.”
“If you return, O Israel … if you put away your abominations from my presence.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to take away what afflicts or defiles his people, sickness, plagues, iniquity, the heart of stone, the reproach of his people; of the people, to put away the evil of their doings.

evidence.note: “I will take sickness away from among you.”
“Pray to Yahweh that he take away the serpents from us.”
Pharaoh: “Plead with Yahweh to take away the frogs.”
“This is all the fruit of taking away (הָסִר) his sin”: quoted at Rom 11:27.
“This is my covenant with them, when I take away (ἀφέλωμαι) their sins.”
“He will swallow up death for ever … and the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth.”
“I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.”
“Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, remove the foreskins of your heart.”
“Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before my eyes.”
“I will smelt away your dross … and remove all your alloy.”
“Yahweh has taken away your judgments … the King of Israel, Yahweh, is in your midst.”
“Remove your stroke from me.”
“Remove vexation from your heart.”

senses.gloss: remove a person or people; depose
senses.definition: To remove someone from a place or office: a king from his throne, a queen mother from her rank, Israel and Judah from Yahweh's face into exile; of Yahweh's favour or justice, to withdraw it.

evidence.note: “Yahweh was very angry with Israel and removed them from his presence; none was left but the tribe of Judah.”
“I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I have removed Israel.”
Asa “removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother.”
The king of Egypt deposed Jehoahaz in Jerusalem.
“Saul removed him (David) from his presence and made him commander of a thousand.”
“As I took it (my steadfast love) from Saul, whom I removed from before you.”
“Remove the turban, take off the crown … until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it” (v. 32).
“Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer or his steadfast love from me.”
“Until I die I will not remove my integrity from me.”
“God has taken away my justice.”

senses.definition: To make something turn from its course: the ark turned aside to another house, a son turned from following Yahweh, the foot turned from evil, the ear from the law; with a negative, to leave nothing out.

evidence.note: David would not take the ark to the city of David, “and David turned it aside (וַיַּטֵּהוּ) to the house of Obed-edom”, with נָטָה for the same act.
“He will turn your son away from following me.”
“Do not incline to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from evil.”
“He who turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.”
“Turn away from me the way of falsehood.”
“Joshua left nothing undone (לֹא הֵסִיר דָּבָר) of all that Yahweh commanded Moses.”
“They shall profane the sanctuary, the fortress, and shall take away the continual (offering), and set up the abomination that makes desolate.”

senses.definition: The passive of the hiphil: the fat removed from the offering, the bread of the presence taken away, the continual offering taken away, a city removed from being a city.

evidence.note: “As the fat is removed from the peace offering.”
“The bread of the presence that was removed from before Yahweh, to put hot bread in its place.”
“Damascus is removed from being a city, and will be a heap of ruins.”
“From the time that the continual is taken away, and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there shall be 1290 days.”

senses.definition: Once: Yahweh turned aside the sufferer's ways, so that he could not keep his course.

evidence.note: “He turned aside (סוֹרֵר) my ways and tore me to pieces; he made me desolate.”

evidence.locator: Psa.6.9, סוּרוּ → ἀπόστητε; Isa.52.11, סוּרוּ → ἀπόστητε; 1Sa.16.14, סָרָה → ἀπέστη; 2Sa.7.15; Dan.11.31; ἀφίστημι renders סוּר ×65

evidence.note: “Depart (ἀπόστητε) from me, all you workers of unrighteousness”: Psa 6:9 in the Septuagint's words.
“Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart (ἀποστήτω) from unrighteousness.”
“An evil heart of unbelief, in departing (ἀποστῆναι) from the living God”, as the heart that turns from Yahweh (Jer 17:5).

evidence.locator: Psa.14.3, סָר → ἐξέκλιναν; Psa.34.15, סוּר → ἔκκλινον; Psa.119.115, סוּרוּ → ἐκκλίνατε; ἐκκλίνω renders סוּר ×22

evidence.note: “All have turned aside (ἐξέκλιναν)”, quoting Psa 14:3.
“Let him turn away (ἐκκλινάτω) from evil and do good”, quoting Psa 34:15.
“Turn away (ἐκκλίνατε) from them”: from those who cause divisions.

evidence.locator: Isa.6.7, סָר → ἀφελεῖ; Isa.25.8, יָסִיר → ἀφεῖλεν; Zec.3.4, הָסִירוּ → ἀφέλετε; Ezk.21.31, הָסִיר → ἀφείλου; ἀφαιρέω renders סוּר ×32

evidence.note: “When I take away (ἀφέλωμαι) their sins”, from Isa 27:9.
“It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away (ἀφαιρεῖν) sins.”

greek.gloss: take off, take away from around

evidence.locator: Exo.34.34, יָסִיר → περιῃρεῖτο; περιαιρέω renders סוּר ×3

evidence.note: “When one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away (περιαιρεῖται)”: Moses removing the veil of Exo 34:34.
Sacrifices “which can never take away (περιελεῖν) sins.”
“When he had removed (μεταστήσας) him (Saul), he raised up David to be their king”: the removal of 2Sa 7:15.
“When I am removed (μετασταθῶ) from the stewardship.”

parallels.note: “Incline, turn aside”: beside סוּר for the same leaving of the path.
“Forsake”: those who turn aside from Yahweh have forsaken him.
“Fear”: to fear Yahweh and to turn from evil are said together.

opposites.note: “Cling, cleave”: Hezekiah clung to Yahweh and did not turn aside.
“Return”: the remedy for having turned aside.
“Do good”: what follows turning from evil.

phrases.gloss: turn aside neither to the right nor to the left
the high places were not removed
he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam

words.summary: Eight times. Mostly “revolt”, a turning aside from Yahweh spoken by a false prophet or added to by the people; once a false charge, once a ceasing. Its sense is the verb's, but the root it is formed from is uncertain: סָרָה could be the feminine of the verb's participle, or a noun of סרר “be stubborn, rebellious”, whose Akkadian cousins mean “false, falsehood”.

senses.definition: A turning aside from Yahweh: spoken by a prophet to turn the people from the way Yahweh commanded, added to by a people who will not be taught, and made deep by Israel.

evidence.note: The prophet “has spoken סָרָה against Yahweh your God … to thrust you from the way in which Yahweh your God commanded you to walk”: a turning from the way.
Hananiah: “This year you shall die, because you have spoken סָרָה against Yahweh.”
The same of Shemaiah the Nehelamite.
“Why will you still be struck? You add revolt (סָרָה).”
“Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted (הֶעְמִיקוּ סָרָה), sons of Israel”: return is the remedy.
“Transgressing and denying Yahweh, and turning back (וְנָסוֹג) from after our God, speaking oppression and revolt.”
“If a malicious witness rises against a man to testify סָרָה against him”: a charge that turns aside from the truth; the witness is false (v. 18).

senses.definition: Once: a turning aside from striking, a let-up.

evidence.note: The king of Babylon, “striking the peoples in wrath with a striking without ceasing (בִּלְתִּי סָרָה)”, parallel “a persecution without restraint (בְּלִי חָשָׂךְ)”.

words.gloss: Sur, a gate of the temple
words.summary: “The gate of Sur”, one of the posts of the guard at the temple when Joash was made king. 2Ch 23:5 has “the gate of the foundation (הַיְסוֹד)” in its place. Whether the name is the verb's “turning aside” is not shown. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: A gate where a third of the guard stood when Joash was made king.

evidence.note: “A third at the gate of Sur, and a third at the gate behind the guards.”
The parallel account has “the gate of the foundation”.

cognates.gloss: turn (a knife on all sides, to examine it); go around, visit, superintend
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Babylonian Talmud: the turning and going around of the same consonants. The Hebrew's sense is the going aside from a course; the Aramaic keeps the turning.

evidence.locator: s.v. סוּר (ch.), O00409, citing Erub. 63a (סַר סכינא, examined the knife), Ḥull. 18a, B. Mets. 76b (Pa., he visited his fields)

cognates.gloss: go, go along, journey; go away, pass away, depart
cognates.note: Root s-y-r, not s-w-r: a going or departing, near the Hebrew's “depart”, but of going in general rather than going aside. Arabic سور s-w-r, the same consonants as the Hebrew, means “leap, spring upon; climb a wall; wall; bracelet” and shares nothing with it.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1483, art. سير, سَارَ (n21410)
evidence.note: “He, or it, went [in any manner, or any pace]; went, or passed, along; marched, journeyed, or proceeded; went away, passed away, or departed.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1464, art. سور, سَارَ (n21203)
evidence.note: s-w-r: “He leaped or sprang”; no turning sense.

cognates.note: A middle-weak verb of the same consonants, of turning round; the Hebrew's turning is out of a course, not round about.

cognates.gloss: falsehood, fraud, crime; (sarru) false, a liar
cognates.note: From sarāru “be false”, a doubled root s-r-r, not s-w-r. It fits the false witness's סָרָה (Deu 19:16) and the false prophet's (Deu 13:6; Jer 28:16), and would put the noun under Hebrew סרר.

doctrine.statement: When Samuel anointed David, “the spirit of Yahweh came upon David from that day forward”, and in the next verse “the spirit of Yahweh departed from Saul” (1Sa 16:13–14). The text then says the same thing without the word spirit: “Yahweh was with him, and had departed from Saul” (1Sa 18:12), and Saul himself, “God has departed from me and does not answer me” (1Sa 28:15–16). Samson's strength would “depart from” him if his head was shaved, and when it was, “he did not know that Yahweh had departed from him” (Jdg 16:17, 20). The bad spirit that troubled Saul was “from Yahweh” and departed when David played (1Sa 16:14, 23). From the verses: the spirit of Yahweh is Yahweh's own power and presence with a man, given and withdrawn by him, not a separate person; its departing is Yahweh's departing.

Yahweh takes sin away: to Isaiah, “your iniquity is taken away (סָר) and your sin atoned for” (Isa 6:7); to Joshua the high priest, the filthy garments removed, “I have taken your iniquity from you” (Zec 3:4); of Jacob, “this is all the fruit of taking away his sin” (Isa 27:9), which Paul reads of Israel's salvation, “this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins” (Rom 11:27). The law's sacrifices could not do it: “it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins” (Heb 10:4, 11). The people's part is to put away: their foreign gods (Jos 24:14; 1Sa 7:3), the evil of their deeds (Isa 1:16), the foreskin of their heart (Jer 4:4); and Yahweh's is to remove the heart of stone and give a heart of flesh (Ezk 36:26). From the verses: forgiveness is the removal of sin by Yahweh himself, through the covenant and the sacrifice that the animal offerings could not be, answered by a people who put away what they turned aside to.

Jacob foretold that “the scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples” (Gen 49:10). Yahweh promised David of his son, “my steadfast love shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul” (2Sa 7:15), and Saul's removal was the making of David king (Act 13:22). When the last king of David's line was taken, the word was, “remove the turban, take off the crown … ruin, ruin, ruin I will make it; this also shall be no more, until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it to him” (Ezk 21:31–32). The angel said of Jesus, “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob for ever” (Luk 1:32–33). From the verses: the throne of David was removed, not abolished, and is held in waiting for the one whose right it is; it is given to Jesus, who will reign on it over Israel and the peoples in the kingdom of God on earth.

“He will swallow up death for ever, and the Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from all faces, and the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth” (Isa 25:8). Paul quotes the first words of this verse of the resurrection: “when this mortal puts on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory” (1Co 15:54), at the coming of Christ, when “those who are Christ's” are raised (1Co 15:23, 52). From the verses: the removal of his people's reproach goes with the end of death, at the resurrection at Christ's return, on “all the earth”.

To fear Yahweh and to turn away from evil are one thing in scripture: Job “feared God and turned away from evil” (Job 1:1), and “the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding” (Job 28:28; Pro 3:7; 16:6). Peter quotes the psalm, “let him turn away from evil and do good” (Psa 34:15; 1Pe 3:11), and Paul, after Moses' “depart from the tents of these wicked men” (Num 16:26), writes, “let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness” (2Ti 2:19). Those who will not depart from evil hear the psalm's words from Jesus: “depart from me, all you workers of unrighteousness” (Psa 6:9; Mat 7:23; Luk 13:27). From the verses: the call to depart from evil now is answered at the judgment, when those who did not are sent to depart.

Daniel saw a time when the sanctuary would be profaned, “and they shall take away the continual and set up the abomination that makes desolate” (Dan 11:31; 12:11). Jesus told his disciples, “when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place … then let those in Judea flee to the mountains” (Mat 24:15–16), and Luke gives the same words as “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near” (Luk 21:20). He said, “this generation shall not pass away until all these things take place” (Mat 24:34). From the verses: the taking away of the continual offering and the desolation were fulfilled when the Roman armies surrounded Jerusalem and the temple was destroyed in AD 70, within that generation.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Left out: the brief's verb-stemless tokens that are other roots: מוּסָר “discipline” (BDB j.ca.ac, root יסר, 30 or so tokens; no yasar entry yet), אָסִיר “prisoner” (Psa 79:11; 102:21, root אסר), and the participles סוֹרֵר of סרר. 1Ki 21:5 רוּחֲךָ סָרָה, filed by BDB under the noun (o.au.ad), is the adjective סַר “sullen” of סרר (1Ki 20:43; 21:4 סַר וְזָעֵף) and belongs there; the 4 qal tokens under o.au.ad (1Sa 16:14, 23; Isa 11:13; Ezk 16:42) are the verb, so lexicon-support's count for the noun is inflated by 5. Jer 6:28 סָרֵי סוֹרְרִים is cited nowhere: “the most stubborn of rebels”, it may be סרר too. The gate name סוּר (o.au.ac) has no bdb key here: the database tags 13 qal infinitives under that key as well, so naming it would count them twice; the name is a place, so it has no name entry, and no personal name is formed from the root (TIPNR has only the place Sur@2Ki.11.6). Open questions: (1) whether סָרָה belongs under סרר rather than סור (Akkadian sartu/sarru “falsehood” is recorded as possible; the false-witness use at Deu 19:16 fits it); (2) the cognates are thin: no Syriac in the Peshitta (SEDRA has no SWR root; SYR is “side”), no Ugaritic consulted (DULAT, not vendored), and Arabic s-y-r “go, depart” is only possible. Jewish Aramaic סוּר “turn” is the one cognate recorded as such. The continual-taken-away doctrine states the AD 70 reading plainly; the reviewer may want to add the 1290 days or the Antiochus question to the note. Septuagint renderings of the noun (ἀσέβεια, ἀνομία, βουλή, ἀνίατος, ἀπειθέω) are scattered and not recorded.
